title: Bending-Active Metal Panel Deformation
summary: Connecting target geometry, opening patterns and elastic sheet behaviour.
yearNote: The thesis chapter is dated 2020; the portfolio index lists 2021.

credits.assembly: Collaborative; individual contributors are not fully identified in the reviewed source.
credits.media: Portfolio evidence credited to Chia-Hsuan Chao as printed. Individual image authorship remains to be confirmed.
credits.sourceEdition: Current role attribution follows the VerFacade portfolio chapter. Displayed source pages come from the earlier 2025 portfolio edition.

overview.introduction: A research story about geometry, openings and the behaviour of a metal sheet.

form.label: FORM
heading: The shape begins
with an opening.
paragraphs: A desired surface is only the beginning. This thesis asks how the geometry of a cut pattern can help a metal sheet take that form.
Miura folding represents the surface’s local angles. Those angles link the overall shape to a repeatable operation at the scale of one opening.
form.aside: A relationship between design intent and material behaviour.

system.label: SYSTEM
heading: From angle
to pattern.
paragraphs: I developed an individual thesis workflow connecting Miura representation, a regression-based opening library and dynamic physical simulation.
The opening values inform a reconstructed mesh. Paired edges then describe how the openings close and the panel bends.
system.footnote: The source workflow, shown here as documentary evidence.

pattern.label: SYSTEM / DETAIL
heading: A local rule.
A different surface.
paragraphs: The research relates opening length and width to bending angle through a sampled function library.
Arc, twist and saddle mock-ups explore how those local relationships accumulate into different surfaces.
pattern.note: The original calibration data and some sampling details remain unresolved. This page does not invent a live predictor.

make.label: MAKE
heading: Sewn into
space.
paragraphs: Pairs of holes and plastic ties close the patterned openings. Panel connections, including rivets, bring the separate sheets into a spatial prototype.
The joints remain visible: the method becomes part of the object’s expression.
make.note: Construction notes describe two workers over three days. These are source reports, not new measurements.

validation.label: EVIDENCE
heading: From simulation
to the made object.
paragraphs: Simulation, 3D scans and physical mock-ups are brought together in the portfolio. The assembled installation makes the research tangible.
The browser shows the supplied final geometry. Its camera, shading and contour treatments explain the surface; they do not calculate a new equilibrium shape.
validation.note: The available evidence does not establish structural certification or universal prediction accuracy.

heading: Intent,
